text:
sarah: Heads-up — customer-ops reported a Private/VPC cluster started failing large-batch inferences after a host kernel security update last night. Several pods show NCCL hangs and occasional cuBLAS mismatches :facepalm:

jamal: any logs? what error codes?

customer-ops: seeing repeated hangs during all-reduce, then GPU processes get killed by OOM killer. nv_peer_mem failed to load on some nodes.

irene: can you paste the driver + cuda reported by the node?

customer-ops: output from node01:
```
# nvidia-smi
Driver Version: 525.116.04
CUDA Version: 11.8
# uname -r
5.15.0-88-generic
# lsmod | grep nvidia
(nothing for nvidia_uvm on problem nodes)
```

ben: looks like kernel update bumped to 5.15.0-88 and DKMS didn't rebuild the nvidia modules — vendor-provided kernel packaging pinned headers or removed linux-headers package. Classic customer-side drift.

sarah: are these nodes fully managed by the customer's infra team? They said they run our Private agent but maintain host OS.

customer-ops: yes, infra owns host lifecycle. They applied a security kernel patch staged from their distro maintainer.

marie: likely mismatch: modules not built for new kernel => UVM missing => NCCL falls back and can deadlock under multi-GPU jobs. We need to confirm whether the driver binary is compatible with current CUDA runtime (sometimes minor driver updates regress ABI).

jamal: can we get the kernel module build logs? Ask them to run:
```
sudo dkms status | grep nvidia || sudo /sbin/dkms autoinstall
journalctl -k -u dkms -n 200
```

customer-ops: dkms status shows no nvidia entries. dkms autoinstall returns no candidates. They don't keep the original dkms package installed (they use a vendor kernel packaging flow).

ben: ok — remediation options: 1) install vendor kernel-headers + rebuild modules, 2) roll back kernel to previous version, 3) install NVIDIA runfile driver that includes prebuilt modules (risky for their change control), 4) route workloads to Dedicated/Hosted while they fix.

irene: for Private customers we need documented guidance and a supported matrix note that vendor-pinned kernels can cause DKMS failures. This isn't a Redwood runtime bug but we should ship better diagnostics and an agent check that detects missing nvidia modules and reports drift to the Console.

infra-bot: created ticket RINF-4221 for oncall triage, linked to customer case #7892.

ops-oncall: triage notes — impact: 3 nodes, ~40% of that customer's throughput, started ~02:14 UTC. Region: eu-west-1 (customer-managed vlan). They requested rollback but patch is security-critical.

sarah: Security patch complicates rollback. Customer asks for a short-term workaround to restore inference while they coordinate with security team.

jamal: quick workaround: cordon problem nodes and move pods to nodes still on old kernel if capacity exists. If not, suggest reducing model concurrency or batch size to avoid all-reduce stress (less likely to hit NCCL). Could also enable NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to avoid some hangs (performance hit).

customer-ops: tried cordon/evict, but cluster is near capacity. Will try NCCL env var and smaller batch size.

marie: longer-term: we should update our Private install docs to recommend keeping dkms packages or recording the driver package used, and surface a "kernel drift" alert in Console with recommended remediation steps. Also add a short note: "If you use vendor kernel packaging, ensure linux-headers and dkms are retained or prebuild modules for all kernel series."

ben: propose change to agent: a nightly host check that captures `uname -r`, `nvidia-smi`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, and whether driver modules match the kernel. If mismatch, raise a ticket and mark nodes 'at-risk' for rolling upgrades.

irene: agree. Also we should add to our supported matrix FAQ: explicitly call out that air-gapped or locked systems that pin kernel packages are unsupported unless they provide prebuilt driver modules for each kernel.

customer-ops: update — setting NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 allowed jobs to finish but performance dropped ~2.5x. They accept that as a temporary mitigation while security team coordinates a rebuild.

sarah: follow-ups: 1) Field Eng to coordinate with customer to help rebuild modules or schedule a controlled kernel rollback where allowed, 2) Devex to add kernel-drift checklist to Private onboarding, 3) Infra to scope agent host-check change (ticket RINF-4223), 4) Docs to add explicit note in Supported Matrix about vendor kernel pinning (PR).

jamal: adding one more gotcha — some older driver versions with new kernels expose subtle cuBLAS mismatches (fp16 kernels). Recommend we ask the customer to test a small canary workload after rebuild before full traffic.

marie: I'll own the docs PR. ben, can you draft the agent host-check prototype?

ben: yes, I'll prototype the check and drop a quick RFC in #eng-infra later today.

ops-oncall: marking thread resolved for now — temporary mitigation accepted. Will reopen if customer reports more failures. :white_check_mark:

sarah: thanks team. Please link back to RINF-4221 and customer case when you update docs/agent tickets.
